about: Derived from recorded runs of TypeSafe's Jev (model jev-1.13.0) through the experiments' reference grader, which kept every raw answer. 'questions': the exact questions that grader built for two rubrics under every framing (its state was {'input', 'submission'}; the values do not affect questions). 'answers': raw answers with the criterion they answered and the verdict (binary) or selected option index (multi-choice) the grader recorded. The recorded grader broke one tie differently: P(yes) exactly at the threshold was MET. It snapped an expected Score to a level with Python's round (half to even), as the library does. Those two rubrics (binary criteria, and ordinal criteria that carry their NA option) and that state are where the grader and the library build identical requests. Elsewhere its requests differed: under ordinal_framing='score' it posed a nominal criterion as a Score too (the library always poses one as a Choice); it sent a criterion's options as given, where the library adds the NA option under auto_na_option=True; its framed instructions had no reference-submission sentence; and it sent a structured submission flattened into 'submission' (the library sends 'thinking' and 'output' and judges the output).
